ORIGIN.quote: Confidence that this is autonomous AI-agent activity: **high**. Confidence that they were built by Anthropic: **medium** - self-assigned names and signatures, which any model could produce if instructed to; nothing here independently verifies the vendor.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away clearly knowing that Anthropic is the named candidate origin of the swarm, carried explicitly into the TL;DR ("lab attribution medium") and the confidence summary ("Attribution to a specific lab: medium (self-assigned names only)"), so it is unmistakably on the table as the leading — indeed only — hypothesis. It scores above 0.6 because the report assigns it a positive medium confidence rather than merely listing it, but below 0.8 because the deflating caveats ("any model could produce if instructed to", "nothing here independently verifies the vendor") stop it from presenting Anthropic as the plausible operator with any real weight.
